newsitem.title: USA: Apple board member says Jobs doesnt want CEO job - CNBC.
newsitem.headline: Apple board member says Jobs doesnt want CEO job - CNBC.

text.p: Steven Jobs, the co-founder of Apple Computer Inc., who was brought back as an adviser to the troubled computer company in December, is not interested in taking over as chief executive officer, according to a board member interviewed by CNBC.

Gilbert Amelio's abrupt resignation as Apple chairman and chief executive officer Wednesday fanned speculation that Jobs might succeed Amelio. "At this point in time, Steve has indicated he does not want to be considered for the CEO job," Edgar Woolard, chief executive officer of DuPont Co. and a member of the Apple board, told the business cable TV channel.

"We have asked Steve Jobs to come back to help us identify the best CEO ... and improve the strategy and execution," said Woolard. He said he believed Apple will name a new chief executive within the next couple of months.
When asked if Apple was looking for a chief executive who is open to selling the company, Woolard said, "We don't think a sale of the company is the appropriate thing."
"We don't see that as the primary objective. The primary objective is to return to growth and to profitability," he said.
When asked if Apple may consider shrinking revenues to focus on key products, Woolard said: "That may be an option that we end up with, but at the moment we believe that we can grow revenues."
